text:
I'll review the staged GUARD plan against the named criteria, starting by checking that the file matches the digest and then reading the custody requirements in full.`plans/phase-plan-v2-GUARD.md` matches digest `d7e3cf7b111ae9f95e7a15e0a3176bd6d8a8e9bde4af1ca702b8bc26a38a45e4` (68351 bytes, 973 lines). The roadmap pin `ee1f3152…` matches `specs/phase-plans-v2.md`. This vote covers that plan text only. SL-0 implementation, SL-2 closeout, release, and the product diff stay outside it. The live helper still uses 20 ms `/proc` ancestry polling; that remains work for implementation.

## IF-0-GUARD-2 and EC-GUARD-1..3

The three criteria are executable, mutually consistent, and falsifiable.

IF-0-GUARD-2 and EC-GUARD-1 freeze one `pnpm verify` command for pull request, main, and release: frozen install, build, lint, typecheck, boundary checks, one admitted disposable database, one root suite, and transport pack smoke. A suppressed exit, a skipped stage, or a publish path that can skip verification or substitute a tarball falsifies the gate. Rehearsal stays dry-run; `id-token: write` stays on the publication job; dispatch publish requires the default branch and a protected ref.

EC-GUARD-2 is proved by `pnpm test:guard` (tooling, setup, and integration IDs) and `pnpm test:integration` (integration IDs only). `verify` and `test:guard` require the six custody IDs in `tests/guard/process.test.ts`. A missing, renamed, skipped, duplicated, or wrong-file custody case fails those commands even when SQL passes. Plain `pnpm test` strips credential and database variables and drops `*.db.test.ts` before collection.

EC-GUARD-3 is the readiness vitest file plus a source-grounded section-6 inventory. The plan states that this file is a documentation check and leaves `pnpm verify` as the custody gate.

## Passive post-exit rule and required cases

Completion classifies an adopted non-payload child by payload pidfd exit-readiness. If a re-poll still shows the payload pidfd unreadable, the launch fails and the whole subtree is drained. If the child is first seen after exit-readiness, the supervisor waits passively until the admitted operation deadline and withholds any supervisor signal before that deadline. Success is allowed only when every adoptee is quiescent by that deadline. A child that needs a signal fails the launch, then uses the original forced drain. A service child still alive at the deadline fails. `T` is 2.5 s: SIGKILL at 500 ms and quiescence within the following 2 s.

The required IDs force those outcomes. `GUARD-CUSTODY-double-fork` keeps the payload alive through a full adoption scan and expects launch failure plus a proved subtree drain. `GUARD-CUSTODY-immediate-orphan` includes a self-exiting post-exit adoptee (success only after passive reap), a long-lived post-exit adoptee (failure), and 100 zero-escape trials. One title per ID matches the duplicate-ID rule, so those oracles sit in the single test the gate requires. `GUARD-CUSTODY-clone-reap`, `GUARD-CUSTODY-thread-leader-exit`, and `GUARD-CUSTODY-hung-child` cover the remaining custody controls. The hung-child control must show validated ADMIT, payload start, and a live descendant; `not_started` fails it. It runs without concurrent test files.

## Legacy positive control

`GUARD-CUSTODY-legacy-positive` keeps the old detector, starts that poll only after the probe parent's exit is pidfd-confirmed, and runs under a test-owned subreaper so the root-suite custodian adopts the child only after the observation. That subreaper holds the adoptee unreaped through the observation, then drains it with pidfds. Ten trials must show at least one marked child absent from the legacy set. A zero-escape run fails the control.

The current `discover()` path skips a parent that is no longer live, so a poll that starts only after pidfd exit-readiness misses children never recorded while the parent was alive. That is a deterministic form of the race in `plans/evidence/v2/reviews/GUARD-immediate-orphan-probe.json` (8 escapes in 10 trials).

## Pre-install client

The custody client is dependency-free Node 24 code, loaded before frozen install and in artifact consumers that reinstall nothing. The specified test runs `verify`'s entrypoint and the artifact verifier in a disposable checkout with no `node_modules`, and READY plus admission precede install and pnpm effects. On this machine, Node v24.13.0 imported `scripts/verify.mjs`, `scripts/verify-publish-artifacts.mjs`, and `tests/helpers/guard-process.ts` through that static graph. Python 3.10.12 provides `os.pidfd_open` and `signal.pidfd_send_signal`, which matches the stated 3.10 floor.

## Root and job deadlines

The reservation formula matches the stated totals. With `T = 2.5` s and `U = 17.5` s, one launcher is 22.5 s or 57.5 s with an ordinary child and 20 s or 55 s without one. Two nested three-slot owners over ordinary work are 112.5 s. The job limit is 20 minutes. The first step stamps `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` and passes cutoff `stamp+17` minutes, leaving a nominal three-minute headroom for that 112.5 s reservation and receipt upload. Standalone `pnpm test` uses a 15-minute lifetime from entry and reserves its forced-drain tail inside that bound. An external kill before a receipt is unproven failure. Insufficient remaining time fails before admission.

## Every-run hosted fixture evidence

Hosted mode fixes the host at `127.0.0.1`, requires `HostIp` `127.0.0.1`, and checks workflow mapping against Docker metadata before SQL admission. A mismatch stops for an amendment. Every hosted run records the mapped host port, Docker HostIp and host-port metadata, their agreement, and the non-loopback refusal control. Cleanup of a runner-owned service is recorded as runner-owned and unobserved. SL-2 keeps the final pull-request-head receipt at `plans/evidence/v2/GUARD-sql-setup.json`, with post-merge evidence stored separately.

## Per-seat provenance

The plan panel and the SL-2 production panel each record model ID, subscription CLI or TUI route, session or invocation ID, verdict, and transcript or output digest. The Claude seat is `claude-opus-5-5` on the subscription TUI. The amendment receipt binds this plan hash, the prior accepted hash, ownership, source and probe hashes, four usable results, dispositions, and the operator platform decision. Historical votes stay on their own hashes.

## Suggestions

These are separate from the acceptance findings.

1. Put pid-and-start liveness in the legacy-positive pass line, alongside absence from the legacy set. The hold-unreaped clause already says the child is still held at observation.
2. Bind the no-`node_modules` READY-before-install check to a required tooling ID so omitting it fails `verify`.
3. Drive the funding check from the external 20-minute deadline as well as `stamp+17` minutes. The plan already says the runner clock can start before the first step, and a service-image pull is the likely consumer of that gap.
4. Name the non-loopback refusal steps and the receipt fields, and fail the hosted job when the uploaded receipt omits port, HostIp, agreement, or that result.
5. State that the long-lived post-exit case keeps the owner waiting through the post-deadline tail `T`, and that its test timeout covers `D+T`. The hung-child control already stacks 250 ms, then 500 ms, then 2 s.

AGREE
